properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on being told that two retirement edges exist and neither is read: \"these are a new type of orphans that I never thought about and curious why until now haven't they surfaced? ... should reflow2 have something that detects these class of orphans, and are there other orphan developments (actually implemented design) that nothing detects or surfaces?\"

⚠️ PROVENANCE CORRECTION FIRST, because he asked what search produced the SUPERSEDES claim and the honest answer is NONE. It was read out of dec:one-retire-edge, which records a schema sweep another session ran on 2026-07-28. It was relayed as though freshly measured. THE MEASUREMENT BELOW WAS THEN ACTUALLY RUN, and it is what this node is for.

=== THE MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-09, against reflow2's own 1,869-node / 7,051-edge design ===

Method, stated because the first cut of it was too crude to trust: an edge type counts as REACHED if it is instantiated in this design, OR named in `structural_rule`'s propagation table (11 edges), OR named anywhere in non-test Rust outside its own `pub const` declaration. Anything failing all three is declared vocabulary with nothing behind it.

EIGHT OF SIXTY EDGE TYPES ARE DECLARED AND UNREACHED ON EVERY TEST:
  COMPLIES_WITH · CONTAINS_EPOCH · EVOLVES_INTO · IMPOSES · MITIGATES · SUPERSEDES · SUPPLEMENTS · VIOLATES_RULE

SEVEN OF TWENTY-NINE NODE TYPES HAVE ZERO INSTANCES HERE:
  Anchor · DimensionAssessment · DimensionObservation · EnvironmentRule · Flow · QualityGate · ReadinessAssessment

FIVE MORE EDGE TYPES ARE INSTANTIATED BUT REACHED ONLY GENERICALLY — not in the propagation table, never named in code: ABOUT_ENTITY (117 instances), CAUSES (9), INTERACTS_WITH (4), OPERATES_IN (3), VALID_TO (2). These are not dead; they are unnamed, which means nothing would notice if they stopped working.

⭐ THREE OF THESE ALREADY HAVE INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, which is why this is a class and not a curiosity:
  - VIOLATES_RULE — dev_storyflow filed it HOURS before this measurement: `describe_schema{from:Component, to:DesignRule}` returns 17 candidates and VIOLATES_RULE is not among them, so a session doing the documented thing cannot discover the edge named for the job. They used VIOLATES instead and said it is presumably wrong.
  - QualityGate — dev_storyflow's governance trial, item ⑦: \"I could not find an honest use, and I think that is informative... Recording the decline, because 'the type exists and nobody instantiated it' is otherwise indistinguishable from nobody having tried.\"
  - Anchor — dec:anchor-retire-or-implement is already OPEN on exactly this: \"superseded by Snapshot but still advertised: retire it or implement it?\"

=== WHY IT NEVER SURFACED, which is his real question ===

EVERY DETECTOR IS INSTANCE-LEVEL AND THIS IS A VOCABULARY-LEVEL FACT. detect_gaps computes over nodes and edges that EXIST — unsatisfied_requirement needs a Requirement, disconnected_community needs a cluster of two or more, orphan_node needs a node. A declared type with zero instances produces NOTHING for any of them to anchor on. The blind spot is not an oversight in any one detector; it is that no detector asks a question ABOUT THE SCHEMA rather than about the design.

⭐⭐ AND THE SHARPEST PART: THE RULE ABOUT UNREAD THINGS IS ITSELF UNREAD. dec:edge-orthogonality is ACCEPTED and says a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT — it is the decision that retired VALIDATES and ENABLES on precisely this reasoning. Nothing computes it. So the principle was applied ONCE, by hand, and the eight above accumulated afterwards with nobody to notice.

=== ARE THERE OTHER UNSURFACED ORPHAN DEVELOPMENTS? YES, AND ONE IS ALREADY OPEN ===

dec:bl-155 (OPEN): \"40 of 132 served tools were never called in the retained sample, and reflow2 cannot tell 'unused' from 'unreachable'.\" That is the same shape one level out — built surface nobody reaches — and it has the same cause: reflow2 measures how well the DESIGN covers the SYSTEM, and never how well anything covers the SURFACE reflow2 itself ships.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each:

(A) A CENSUS REPORT, NOT A GAP — a `vocabulary_census` naming declared-but-unreached types, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. CHEAPEST, and it cannot false-positive into nagging. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is the same failure one level along; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen.

(B) A GAP AT LOW SEVERITY — `unreached_vocabulary`, one per declared type with nothing behind it, acknowledgeable. Makes it appear in the loop where people already look. COUNTER, AND IT IS SERIOUS: a demonstrator legitimately does not use Flow or ReadinessAssessment, so this would fire on correct work in every young design — the exact thing dec:read-hint-shape and the phase-nudge doctrine were built to avoid. Firing on the SCHEMA (a fixed 60/29) rather than on the user's design might dodge that, since it is reflow2's own vocabulary being judged rather than the consumer's modelling.

(C) SCOPE IT TO THE SHIPPED SURFACE ONLY — make it reflow2's own maintenance instrument (a tools/ script, like toolsnap), not a served capability. Honest about who the finding is for: a consumer does not care that reflow2 declares SUPPLEMENTS, and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party would ask what the CONSUMER gets. COUNTER: the consumer DOES get something — describe_schema offers them these types, and VIOLATES_RULE proves a consumer can waste time on one.

(D) DO NOTHING NEW AND JUST PRUNE — decide dec:one-retire-edge and dec:anchor-retire-or-implement, delete what loses, and accept that the next accumulation goes unnoticed too. COUNTER: this is exactly what happened after dec:edge-orthogonality, and eight more arrived.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, whichever is chosen: another marker nothing reads. That is the finding this node is about, and it would be a fourth instance of it.

BOUND, stated rather than glossed: this measured ONE design — reflow2's own. A type with zero instances HERE may be in daily use in dev_storyflow or flo2, and the census would need to be per-design to mean anything to a consumer. The 8 unreached-on-every-test edges are the stronger claim, because those have no code behind them anywhere and that is a property of the SHIPPED BUILD rather than of this graph.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 detect DECLARED-BUT-UNREACHED vocabulary, when its own accepted rule that a distinction must earn its keep is itself unread?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted without Anthony's word.

The provenance correction is inside the decision text rather than only in conversation, because the claim that started this thread was relayed from another session's sweep as if freshly measured, and a later reader deserves to know which parts were measured today and which were quoted. The measurement in this node WAS run today, with its method stated so it can be re-run or disputed.

Kept separate from dec:one-retire-edge (which asks which of two edges survives) and dec:bl-155 (which asks the same question about served TOOLS): this one asks whether the class should be DETECTED at all. Linked to both rather than merged, because a node holding all three could only ever be part-answered.
